skills.bb-local-toolkit: TRIGGER — need the exact local binary path, install command, venv activate line, or wordlist location for a tool already decided on (ffuf, httpx, subfinder, katana, gau, bbcurl, cbh, Burp MCP, SecLists, …), or need to know whether a tool is installed here at all before writing a command around it. SKIP — bug-bounty when the question is 'what should I test' (bug-class routing), not 'where is the tool on disk'; web2-recon when the ask is the recon pipeline sequence itself rather than one tool's path.
skills.bb-methodology: TRIGGER — start of any hunting session; switching targets; feeling lost about what to do next; asking 'what should I do next' or 'where am I in the process'. Master orchestrator: 5-phase workflow plus critical-thinking framework, routes to hunt-* skills by phase. SKIP — once the vuln class is already identified (e.g. Host header reflects into a JS src URL) load the matching hunt-* skill directly instead of the orchestrator; don't keep this loaded once routing is done, it costs context with no further value.
skills.bb-parallel-roles: TRIGGER — you want more than one mind on the target at once: a plan queue to fan out, recon to keep running while you exploit, a second opinion before a submit, several hosts to cover in parallel, or a background learning loop while you hunt. SKIP — you are doing a single focused probe (just do it); you are answering an operator question outside a hunt (the session is idle, no pipeline needed); scope or identity is still unknown (resolve that first — parallelism multiplies whatever you already have, including the mistakes).
skills.bug-bounty: TRIGGER — topic-match routing: need a short list of the 2-3 relevant hunt-* skills for a target, or general 'what bug classes apply here' guidance. Orchestrator only — hands off to hunt-dispatch (engagement-mode fingerprint), web2-recon/offensive-osint (recon execution), triage-validation then report-writing (finding pipeline). SKIP — bb-local-toolkit when the question is a concrete tool/wordlist path, not bug-class routing; don't load every hunt-* simultaneously — pick 2-3 by topic match and close this skill once routed.
skills.bugcrowd-reporting: TRIGGER — filing a Bugcrowd submission; VRT category has no exact match; triager closed a report as OOS or downgraded severity; cross-referencing a chained submission; scope splits QA vs production. SKIP — report-writing for platform-agnostic body/tone/CVSS scoring; triage-validation for the pre-submit correctness gate (run that first — this skill only covers Bugcrowd-specific presentation on top of an already-validated finding).
skills.evidence-hygiene: TRIGGER — before capturing any PoC screenshot or video; before attaching a HAR file; whenever evidence will contain session cookies, auth tokens, or another user's PII. SKIP — report-writing/bugcrowd-reporting for how to write the report body itself — this skill only covers capture and redaction of the evidence attached to it.
skills.hunt-anomaly: TRIGGER — you need findings that no hunt-* class will name for you: the app believes a header, an older API still answers, a status is client-writable, a safe method fires an action, an answer never moves no matter the input. SKIP — you already know the class and it has a skill (use hunt-idor / hunt-sqli / hunt-ssrf …); hunt-differential once the question is specifically 'do these two states disagree', hunt-invariants once the question is specifically 'can I make money or state impossible'.
skills.hunt-api-misconfig: TRIGGER — an API response includes fields beyond what the request should expose (mass assignment candidate); a JWT appears in a header/cookie (decode at jwt.io — check alg=none, weak HMAC, kid path traversal, JWK injection); a JSON merge / Object.assign / lodash _.merge takes attacker-controlled keys (prototype-pollution candidate via __proto__); verb-tampering suspected (GET bypassing a POST-only CSRF-protected endpoint, TRACE enabled). SKIP — hunt-cors for Access-Control-*/CORS header issues (owned there, not here); hunt-graphql for GraphQL-specific IDOR/authz; hunt-idor for a plain object-reference bug with no JSON-merge, JWT, or verb-tampering component.
skills.hunt-aspnet: TRIGGER — target fingerprints as ASP.NET Webforms/WCF (`.aspx`/`.asmx`/`.svc` paths, `X-AspNet-Version` or `X-Powered-By: ASP.NET` headers, a `__VIEWSTATE` field present). Covers ViewState deserialization, machineKey recovery, request-validator bypass, trace.axd/elmah.axd disclosure, customErrors stack-trace leaks. SKIP — hunt-sharepoint once SharePoint-specific headers/paths (`_layouts/15/`, `SPRequestGuid`) confirm a SharePoint farm rather than bare Webforms; hunt-deserialization for non-ViewState .NET BinaryFormatter gadget chains.
skills.hunt-ato: TRIGGER — assessing account-takeover potential across a whole auth flow, or chaining 2+ primitives (cookie theft + password oracle + no step-up, lax redirect_uri, dangling-CNAME at redirect_uri) toward a Critical. SKIP — go straight to the single-path skill when only one primitive is in play: hunt-mfa-bypass (MFA-only), hunt-oauth (OAuth-only), hunt-saml (SAML-only), hunt-session (fixation/invalidation only) — use this skill when combining 2+ of those into a demonstrated takeover.
skills.hunt-auth-bypass: TRIGGER — an authentication check can be skipped or circumvented outright: a legacy/unbranded endpoint is reachable without going through the SSO/branded-UI flow (e.g. XMLRPC), a JWT `aud`/audience isn't validated across tenants, or a partner portal accepts an assertion issued for a different IdP. SKIP — hunt-saml for SAML-assertion-internal attacks (XSW, signature stripping/relocation, NameID comment injection) once a `/saml` or ACS endpoint is confirmed; hunt-oauth for OAuth-flow-specific bugs (redirect_uri, state, scope); hunt-mfa-bypass for MFA-step-specific bypass.
skills.hunt-auth0: TRIGGER — login redirects to `https://<tenant>.<region>.auth0.com/authorize`, client bundle references `auth0-js`/`@auth0/auth0-spa-js`/`auth0-react`, or `/.well-known/openid-configuration` resolves on an `auth0.com` domain. Covers Auth0 tenant misconfiguration (Rules/Actions claim injection, callback-URL wildcards, MFA gaps, Organizations cross-tenant leaks) and how downstream APIs validate Auth0-issued tokens (audience/scope confusion). SKIP — hunt-oauth for the generic OAuth/OIDC flow class (redirect_uri, state, PKCE) shared by any provider; hunt-saml if the same tenant also exposes a SAML connection/ACS endpoint; hunt-mfa-bypass once the finding is purely the MFA-step gap with no Auth0-tenant-config component.
skills.hunt-brute-force: TRIGGER — a login/OTP/2FA/password-reset-token field shows no visible lockout; error-string, status-code, or timing differences distinguish valid from invalid usernames; X-Forwarded-For or a similar header is accepted for per-IP rate limiting. SKIP — hunt-mfa-bypass when the OTP entropy/rate-limit gap chains specifically into an MFA-bypass-to-ATO path rather than standalone brute-force; hunt-race-condition when the exploit needs concurrent requests rather than raw high-volume guessing.
skills.hunt-business-logic: TRIGGER — a workflow trusts client-supplied state it shouldn't (price/quantity/discount fields, checkout amount, coupon re-application, a stale/archived price reference), or a multi-step process can be reordered, skipped, or repeated for an unintended benefit. SKIP — hunt-race-condition when the bug needs concurrent requests (double-redemption via timing) rather than a single-request logic flaw; hunt-idor when the issue is purely 'wrong object ID returns unauthorized data' with no financial/state-manipulation component.
skills.hunt-cache-poison: TRIGGER — app sits behind a CDN/reverse-proxy (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai, GCP) and a request header (X-Forwarded-Host, X-HTTP-Method-Override) or an unkeyed cache input might get reflected into a cached response; suspected Web Cache Deception via path/extension confusion. SKIP — hunt-host-header for Host-header attacks that reach SSRF/password-reset/OAuth rather than a cached response; hunt-http-smuggling when the root cause is CL/TE parsing disagreement rather than a cache-key mismatch.
skills.hunt-cors: TRIGGER — a response includes `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`/`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` headers, especially reflecting Origin or `null`; testing an SPA or API that makes cross-origin credentialed requests; a postMessage handler is present. SKIP — hunt-api-misconfig for JWT/mass-assignment/verb-tampering issues found alongside CORS; hunt-dom for a postMessage bug with no CORS/credential component (missing origin check in a `message` listener, not an HTTP CORS header).
skills.hunt-cspt: TRIGGER — JS source (fetch()/XHR/axios call) concatenates attacker-controlled input unencoded into the URL PATH segment (not the query string). SKIP — hunt-open-redirect once the traversal lands on a full off-origin URL redirect rather than a same-origin fetch path; hunt-xss/hunt-dom once the endpoint reached by the traversal leads directly to script execution — log the confirmed chain there instead.
skills.hunt-csrf: TRIGGER — a state-changing request (POST/PUT/DELETE, GraphQL mutation) has no anti-CSRF token, or the token/SameSite/Origin check looks bypassable (subdomain sibling, path-traversal in the token check, text/plain content-type). SKIP — hunt-session for session-fixation/invalidation issues with no forged-cross-site-request component; hunt-websocket for CSWSH (WebSocket-handshake CSRF) specifically.
skills.hunt-deserialization: TRIGGER — target runs Java (gadget-chain candidate for ysoserial), PHP serialize()/unserialize(), Python pickle.loads, .NET BinaryFormatter, or Ruby Marshal.load; a cookie/parameter looks like a serialized blob (base64 `rO0`, `O:`, `\x80\x04`). SKIP — hunt-aspnet for ASP.NET ViewState specifically (its own signed/encrypted format, not raw BinaryFormatter); hunt-rce once a working gadget chain is confirmed and the next step is escalation/impact rather than the deserialization primitive itself.
skills.hunt-differential: TRIGGER — you need a finding and the honest way to get one is to hold everything still and move exactly one dimension: role A vs role B, with auth vs without, /v2 vs /v1, declared vs observed, valid input vs garbage. SKIP — you are hunting a known class and already have a payload list (use that hunt-* skill); hunt-anomaly when the question is open-ended 'what does not add up', hunt-auth-bypass when the axis is specifically authentication, hunt-idor when the axis is specifically object ownership and the object is named.
skills.hunt-dispatch: TRIGGER — internal use only: invoked right after `/hunt` receives a box answer (blackbox|greybox), to fingerprint the target and load the matching framework/stack skill set. SKIP — not for direct user invocation; if unsure what to test, use bb-methodology instead.
skills.hunt-dom: TRIGGER — the bug needs no server round-trip: HTML/attribute injection that could overwrite a JS global (DOM Clobbering), a `message` event listener with no origin check, a Service Worker intercepting same-origin requests, or CSS-selector-based attribute exfiltration. SKIP — hunt-xss for server-reflected/stored injection that then runs in the DOM; hunt-cors for postMessage-adjacent issues that are actually CORS-header-based rather than the listener itself.
skills.hunt-file-upload: TRIGGER — any `/upload`, `/avatar`, `/profile-picture`, `/attachment`, or `/import` endpoint accepts a file. SKIP — hunt-xxe once the uploaded format is XML-based (DOCX/PPTX/SVG-with-XXE) and the exploit path is XML parsing rather than extension/content-type bypass; hunt-ssti if the uploaded file is a server-side template that gets rendered, not stored/executed as a plain file.
skills.hunt-firebase: TRIGGER — target's client bundle initializes `firebase.apps`/`firebaseConfig` (apiKey, authDomain, projectId), or requests hit `firestore.googleapis.com`, `<project>.firebaseio.com`, or `storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/`. Covers Firestore/Realtime Database security-rule bypass, Cloud Storage exposure, Cloud Functions trusting client input over `context.auth`, and ID-token/App-Check confusion. SKIP — hunt-supabase/hunt-auth0 for other BaaS/IdP stacks; hunt-api-misconfig once the bug is a generic JWT/mass-assignment issue with no Firebase-rules component.
skills.hunt-graphql: TRIGGER — target exposes a `/graphql` endpoint or Apollo/Relay client code; testing `node()`/global-ID resolvers, batch queries, or mutation-level authorization. SKIP — hunt-idor for REST-style object-reference bugs with no GraphQL layer; hunt-sqli/hunt-nosqli once a resolver argument reaches a raw DB query — the root cause is the injection class, not GraphQL authz.
skills.hunt-grpc: TRIGGER — target exposes port 50051/443/8443/9090 over HTTP/2, grpcurl/grpcui shows server reflection enabled, or recon reveals a microservice mesh behind Envoy/grpc-gateway. SKIP — hunt-http-smuggling for HTTP/1.1-vs-backend desync issues (different transport-layer bug class); hunt-api-misconfig once gRPC-Web/grpc-gateway transcoding exposes a REST-shaped JSON endpoint with its own authz gaps.
skills.hunt-header-injection: TRIGGER — a response header's value visibly moves with request input (query/body/cookie echoed into `Set-Cookie`/`Location`/`Content-Type`/`Content-Disposition`/`Link`/custom `X-*`), or a request header (Referer, X-Forwarded-*) is re-emitted into a response/log/email. Covers CRLF response splitting, Host/X-Forwarded-Host confusion, cookie/Set-Cookie manipulation, forwarding-header spoofing, and content-type/encoding confusion as one unified normalization-failure class. SKIP — hunt-host-header once the specific chain is Host-header→SSRF/password-reset/OAuth (deeper on that one path); hunt-cache-poison once impact is specifically a poisoned CDN cache rather than the header-injection entry point; hunt-http-smuggling for the CL/TE request-framing-desync primitive specifically; hunt-csrf/hunt-cors for header-adjacent bugs with no injection component.
skills.hunt-host-header: TRIGGER — a forgot-password email builds an absolute link from the Host header; the app sits behind a CDN/reverse-proxy that may leave Host unkeyed in the cache; an OAuth/OIDC endpoint builds redirect_uri or issuer from Host; the app forwards X-Original-URL/X-Rewrite-URL. SKIP — hunt-cache-poison once confirmed impact is a cached response for other users rather than SSRF/ATO/OAuth poisoning; hunt-ssrf once routing-based SSRF via Host is the primary path — this skill covers the Host-header entry point, hunt-ssrf covers exploiting the resulting internal request.
skills.hunt-http-smuggling: TRIGGER — target sits behind a CDN/reverse-proxy plus origin stack (load balancer, WAF) where front-end and back-end might disagree on Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding; Burp HTTP Request Smuggler / smuggler.py is viable. SKIP — hunt-cache-poison once smuggling is confirmed and being chained specifically into cached-response poisoning — log that chain step there; hunt-host-header for Host-based routing/cache issues with no CL/TE desync involved.
skills.hunt-idor: TRIGGER — an endpoint takes a user-controllable identifier (numeric ID, UUID, filename, order/invoice number) in a URL, body, or header and returns or modifies data scoped to a user or tenant. SKIP — hunt-graphql once the identifier is a GraphQL global ID / `node()` argument; hunt-business-logic once access is technically authorized but the *logic* (price, quantity, workflow state) is what's actually broken, not the object reference.
skills.hunt-invariants: TRIGGER — the target moves money, quota, entitlement or workflow state, and the question is whether you can make something impossible happen: a negative balance, a double-applied refund, a discount larger than the cart, a revoked share that still opens, a cancelled order that transitions again. SKIP — the bug is object access rather than object state (hunt-idor); the bug is a class with payloads (use that hunt-* skill); you are still mapping surface (bb-methodology).
skills.hunt-laravel: TRIGGER — target fingerprints as Laravel (`X-Powered-By`, `laravel_session` cookie, `/storage/` paths, Blade error pages). Covers APP_DEBUG stack-trace/env leaks, Telescope/Horizon dashboards, Ignition RCE, signed-URL tampering, Eloquent mass assignment. SKIP — hunt-deserialization for the general PHP-object-injection primitive once it's not Laravel-cookie-specific; hunt-api-misconfig for mass-assignment findings on non-Laravel/generic ORMs.
skills.hunt-ldap: TRIGGER — target authenticates against LDAP/Active Directory (corporate SSO with a directory backend), exposes an address-book/people-search API, or an XML data store queried with XPath. SKIP — hunt-sqli/hunt-nosqli once the backend is confirmed relational/NoSQL rather than a directory service; hunt-ntlm-info for the anonymous NTLM Type-2 AD-topology leak specifically (different primitive, same AD context).
skills.hunt-lfi: TRIGGER — a parameter or path controls which file/template the server reads or includes (`?page=`, `?template=`, `?file=`), or the app uses `include()`/`require()`/similar with user input. SKIP — hunt-file-upload once the traversal target is an uploaded file's stored path rather than a generic include parameter; hunt-rce once LFI is confirmed and the next step is escalating to code execution via log/session poisoning — log the escalation there.
skills.hunt-llm-ai: TRIGGER — target has an LLM-backed feature — chatbot, RAG/summarizer, agentic copilot, MCP tool integration, or any endpoint that runs a document/webpage/email through a model. SKIP — hunt-graphql/hunt-api-misconfig for the underlying API authz once an 'IDOR-via-AI' cross-tenant leak turns out to be a plain object-reference bug wearing an AI-feature costume. Confabulation (the model just being wrong) is never itself a finding.
skills.hunt-mfa-bypass: TRIGGER — tracing an auth flow with a 2FA/OTP/MFA step: check whether MFA is enforced as middleware vs per-endpoint, whether the post-login URL is reachable by direct navigation, whether an OTP code can be replayed or brute-forced, whether recovery codes leak via `/api/me`. SKIP — hunt-ato once 2+ primitives are chained into a demonstrated takeover — log the full chain there instead; hunt-brute-force for pure high-volume credential guessing with no MFA-step component.
skills.hunt-misc: TRIGGER — a finding doesn't cleanly fit any other hunt-* class (miscellaneous disclosed-report patterns with no dedicated skill). SKIP — check whether a dedicated hunt-* skill name already matches the observed bug class first; load this only as a fallback after that check comes up empty.
skills.hunt-nextjs: TRIGGER — target fingerprints as Next.js 13/14/15 (`_next/` paths, `x-powered-by: Next.js`, RSC payloads). Covers Server Actions, Middleware auth-bypass via static-asset paths, ISR cache poisoning, `/_next/image` SSRF. SKIP — hunt-nodejs for generic Node/Express bugs not specific to the Next.js routing/rendering layer; hunt-cache-poison for CDN-level (not ISR-level) cache poisoning.
skills.hunt-nodejs: TRIGGER — target fingerprints as Node.js/Express/Fastify/NestJS/Koa (`X-Powered-By: Express`, stack traces referencing `node_modules`). Covers prototype pollution to RCE, trust-proxy misconfig, child_process/eval injection, template-engine SSTI. SKIP — hunt-nextjs once the framework is specifically Next.js (more specific skill takes priority); hunt-ssti once an EJS/Pug/Handlebars injection is confirmed and the work is escalating the template engine rather than general Node hardening.
skills.hunt-nosqli: TRIGGER — target uses MongoDB/Mongoose, CouchDB, or Redis, or a query parameter accepts a raw operator object (e.g. $gt/$ne/$where) into a filter/where field. SKIP — hunt-sqli once the backend is confirmed relational (Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL/Oracle) rather than NoSQL; hunt-graphql once the injectable argument sits inside a GraphQL resolver — log the DB-layer finding there instead, since query construction differs.
skills.hunt-ntlm-info: TRIGGER — target returns `WWW-Authenticate: NTLM` or `Negotiate` anonymously on an internet-facing IIS/SharePoint/Exchange endpoint. SKIP — hunt-sharepoint once the same host also exposes `/_layouts/15/` or SharePoint-specific headers (chain both, but log the SharePoint attack surface there); hunt-ldap for AD/directory-backend attacks beyond the anonymous Type-2 handshake leak.
skills.hunt-oauth: TRIGGER — target implements OAuth2/OIDC (`/authorize`, `/token`, a `redirect_uri` parameter present). SKIP — hunt-saml once the SSO protocol is confirmed SAML rather than OAuth/OIDC; hunt-ato once an OAuth bug (lax redirect_uri, account-link CSRF) is being chained into a full takeover — log the chain there.
skills.hunt-open-redirect: TRIGGER — a parameter (`?redirect=`, `?next=`, `?return_url=`) or a JS `location`/meta-refresh assignment takes a URL and the app doesn't validate it's same-origin. SKIP — hunt-oauth once the redirect target is specifically an OAuth `redirect_uri` (log there — impact/severity framing differs); hunt-cspt once the traversal is same-origin path manipulation rather than an off-origin URL.
skills.hunt-race-condition: TRIGGER — a limited-use resource (coupon, gift-card balance, OTP attempt, invite, vote) is checked-then-updated in a way that could race under concurrent or HTTP/2-single-packet requests. SKIP — hunt-business-logic for single-request logic flaws with no concurrency component; hunt-brute-force for straightforward high-volume sequential guessing with no timing/TOCTOU angle.
skills.hunt-rce: TRIGGER — a confirmed primitive (deserialization, LFI, SSTI, file upload, command injection) is being escalated to actual code execution, or the target exposes a known 1-day RCE (unpatched CVE with public PoC). SKIP — the specific primitive skill (hunt-deserialization, hunt-lfi, hunt-ssti, hunt-file-upload) for finding/confirming the entry point itself; use this skill once the entry point is confirmed and the goal is proving `whoami`-level execution.
skills.hunt-saml: TRIGGER — target exposes `/saml`, `/Shibboleth.sso`, `/sso/saml/`, an ADFS endpoint, or an AssertionConsumerService URL. SKIP — hunt-auth-bypass once the bypass doesn't touch SAML assertion internals (e.g. a legacy non-SSO endpoint reachable directly); hunt-ato once a SAML bug (XSW, signature stripping) is confirmed and being chained into a demonstrated takeover.
skills.hunt-session: TRIGGER — testing login/logout/password-change/email-change for session regeneration, invalidation, or JWT-as-session expiry/revocation; comparing two real sessions (attacker + victim). SKIP — hunt-csrf for forged-request issues with no session-lifecycle component; hunt-mfa-bypass for MFA-step-specific session gaps (post-MFA state reachable without completing the challenge).
skills.hunt-sharepoint: TRIGGER — target shows SharePoint headers (`SPRequestGuid`, `X-MS-InvokeApp`, `MicrosoftSharePointTeamServices`) or paths (`/_layouts/15/`, `/_vti_bin/`, `/_api/`, `/_catalogs/`). SKIP — hunt-aspnet for bare Webforms/WCF surface with no SharePoint-specific paths; hunt-ntlm-info for the anonymous NTLM Type-2 leak alone, without SharePoint farm-specific enumeration.
skills.hunt-source-aware-sast: TRIGGER — `/hunt` runs with `--source-code <path>` (repository available, not just the live endpoint). Covers the coordinated static-triage baseline (semgrep + ast-grep + gitleaks/trufflehog + trivy fs) that ranks source for dynamic follow-up, plus dependency/lockfile CVE scanning (SCA) as a documented exception to the dynamic-PoC rule. SKIP — bb-local-toolkit for a single tool's install path/flags in isolation; this skill is the coordinated white-box workflow, not a tool reference. hunt-* class skills still own the actual exploitation once static triage points at a candidate.
skills.hunt-source-leak: TRIGGER — start of every recon session, before deep manual testing: check for `.js.map`, `/swagger.json`/`/openapi.json`, `.env`/`.git`, webpack chunks, `robots.txt`/`security.txt`, `asset-manifest.json`. SKIP — web2-recon for the broader subdomain/URL-discovery pipeline this feeds into; hunt-api-misconfig once a leaked route/secret is being exploited rather than just discovered.
skills.hunt-springboot: TRIGGER — target fingerprints as Spring Boot (`X-Application-Context` header, `/actuator/*` paths, Whitelabel Error Page, Java stack traces). SKIP — hunt-deserialization for generic Java gadget chains not reached via Spring-specific Actuator/SpEL surface; hunt-laravel/hunt-nodejs/hunt-aspnet once the framework fingerprint points elsewhere.
skills.hunt-sqli: TRIGGER — a parameter reaches a relational-DB query (Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL/Oracle/Salesforce SOQL) — error messages, timing differences, or ORM raw-fragment usage (Django `.extra()`, Sequelize `literal()`) suggest unsanitized input reaching SQL. SKIP — hunt-nosqli once the backend is confirmed MongoDB/CouchDB/Redis; hunt-graphql once the injectable argument is a GraphQL resolver parameter — log the injection there, since the discovery path differs.
skills.hunt-ssrf: TRIGGER — a parameter or feature makes a server-side outbound request from attacker-influenced input (URL fetch, webhook, PDF/screenshot generator, link-preview, import-from-URL), and the target runs on cloud infra (AWS/GCP/Azure) or an internal network with reachable admin/metadata services. SKIP — hunt-host-header once the SSRF is routed via the Host header specifically rather than a URL parameter; hunt-cspt once the 'traversal' is same-origin path manipulation in a JS fetch call rather than a genuine server-side request.
skills.hunt-ssti: TRIGGER — user input is composed into a string before server-side template rendering (email templates, PDF/report generators, CMS preview, error pages); a `{{7*7}}`/`${7*7}` probe returns `49` or an engine-specific error. SKIP — hunt-nodejs once the confirmed engine is EJS/Pug/Handlebars on a Node stack (log there for stack-specific escalation); hunt-rce once an engine-specific RCE gadget is confirmed and the work is proving code execution.
skills.hunt-subdomain: TRIGGER — recon turns up a CNAME pointing at a cloud/SaaS provider (Azure, Zendesk, Vercel, Fastly, S3) with no live resource behind it, or an OAuth `redirect_uri` points at a dangling subdomain. SKIP — hunt-tls-network for DNS/cert misconfig with no dangling-CNAME/provider-fingerprint takeover angle; hunt-ato once a takeover is confirmed and being chained into email-interception/password-reset ATO.
skills.hunt-supabase: TRIGGER — target's requests hit `<ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/`, `/rest/v1/rpc/`, `/storage/v1`, `/graphql/v1`, `/auth/v1`, or `wss://<ref>.supabase.co/realtime/v1`; client bundle contains a Supabase `anon` key. Covers Row Level Security (RLS) gaps, unsafe `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs, leaked `service_role` keys, lax Storage policies, and Edge Functions trusting headers without binding to issuer/audience/tenant. SKIP — hunt-firebase/hunt-auth0 for other BaaS/IdP stacks; hunt-graphql for the general GraphQL class once the bug isn't RLS-specific (pg_graphql inherits RLS, so most Supabase GraphQL bugs ARE RLS bugs — check here first).
skills.hunt-tls-network: TRIGGER — during recon, evaluating a target's TLS/DNS posture: cipher suites, cert validity, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, AXFR zone transfer, dangling CNAME, CAA records. SKIP — hunt-subdomain once a dangling CNAME is confirmed exploitable (do the takeover there); treat missing-HSTS/missing-CAA/self-signed-cert-with-no-MITM-position as non-findings rather than invoking either skill.
skills.hunt-trusted-header-auth: TRIGGER — the app decides WHO you are from a request header instead of from a session/token: `X-User-Id`, `X-Remote-User`, `X-Authenticated-User`, `X-Consumer-*` (Kong), `X-Auth-Request-Email` (oauth2-proxy), `X-Amzn-Oidc-Identity` (ALB), `X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email` (IAP), `CF-Access-Authenticated-User-Email`, `X-Forwarded-Client-Cert` (mTLS/Envoy), or a carrier/subscriber header (`X-MSISDN`, `X-Subscriber-Id`, `X-Up-Calling-Line-Id`). Also fires when an API returns your own account data with NO cookie/Authorization at all — something else identified you. SKIP — hunt-header-injection when the header value is reflected/injected into a RESPONSE header (CRLF, cache key) rather than trusted as identity; hunt-idor when identity is established correctly and only the object reference is unchecked; hunt-api-misconfig for JWT-internal flaws (alg=none, kid traversal) where the token itself is the identity carrier.
skills.hunt-websocket: TRIGGER — target opens `ws://`/`wss://` connections, uses socket.io/SignalR/Phoenix Channels, or has chat/live-dashboard/trading features. SKIP — hunt-csrf for the general cross-site forged-request pattern once the specific mechanism is confirmed as CSWSH (log the WebSocket-specific handshake finding here instead); hunt-cors for HTTP-header-based cross-origin issues with no WebSocket handshake involved.
skills.hunt-xss: TRIGGER — user input is reflected or stored into an HTML response, especially in admin panels, payment/checkout flows, SSO/signin pages, or collaborative content (wikis/comments/markdown). SKIP — hunt-dom once the sink is purely client-side (DOM Clobbering, postMessage, Service Worker) with no server-side reflection/storage; hunt-cspt once the injection point is a JS fetch() path built from unencoded input rather than an HTML sink.
skills.hunt-xxe: TRIGGER — an endpoint parses XML or an XML-based format (SVG upload, DOCX/PPTX/Office docs, SOAP, SAML ACS) and the parser might resolve external entities. SKIP — hunt-file-upload for non-XML upload-bypass techniques (double extension, magic bytes) on the same endpoint; hunt-saml once the XXE vector is specifically the SAML AssertionConsumerService — log there for the SSO-specific chain.
skills.poc-runtime: TRIGGER — a manual curl/browser PoC just confirmed a candidate finding and Q1/Q6 of the 7-Question Gate need a captured, re-playable artifact instead of a remembered response; before /validate on anything status-code- or body-content-dependent. SKIP — triage-validation for the gate questions themselves (this only produces the evidence one of them needs); evidence-hygiene once the artifact needs screenshot/HAR redaction rather than a raw HTTP capture; hunt-race-condition or hunt-brute-force once the goal is genuinely concurrent/high-volume requests, not single-shot validation.
skills.report-writing: TRIGGER — after a finding has passed validation (triage-validation) and before submitting to H1/Bugcrowd/Intigriti/Immunefi. SKIP — triage-validation if the finding hasn't been through the 7-Question Gate yet (do that first); bugcrowd-reporting for Bugcrowd-specific VRT/severity-override tactics layered on top of this skill's platform-agnostic body.
skills.security-arsenal: TRIGGER — need a specific payload/bypass string (XSS/SSRF/SQLi/XXE/NoSQLi/command-injection/SSTI/IDOR/path-traversal/smuggling/WebSocket/MFA), a gf pattern name, or a check against the always-rejected list before spending time on a lead. SKIP — the matching hunt-* skill for the surrounding methodology/detection context; this skill is payload/reference lookup only, not the hunting approach itself.
skills.triage-validation: TRIGGER — before writing any report: run the 7-Question Gate and 4 pre-submission gates on a candidate finding. SKIP — report-writing once all gates pass (write the report there); security-arsenal to check the always-rejected list first if the finding looks borderline.
skills.web2-recon: TRIGGER — starting recon on a new web2 target, or asked about asset discovery/subdomain enum/attack-surface mapping. SKIP — hunt-source-leak for source-map/`.env`/`.git`/webpack-chunk leakage specifically (run alongside, not instead); bb-local-toolkit for the exact local binary path of a tool named here.
